text:
Columbus remade itself around a summer blockbuster, sending Kirill Marchenko to Toronto for Matthew Knies, and Knies has given the Blue Jackets their best moments, including a winning return to Toronto that NHL.com titled "Knies returns to The Six for a dramatic win." The standings have not followed. Rick Bowness's team is 9-14-1, 2-7-1 over its last ten and winless in three.

Our numbers say the record is worse than the hockey. Columbus gets 49% of the expected goals at five on five and won the chance battle over those last three games (53%), but it has scored about 14 fewer goals than its chances deserve, the biggest finishing hole in our tables this season. Charlie Coyle sums it up: 2 points in his last 10 games on 7.9 expected. That kind of drought rarely lasts.

The goaltending is not the problem. Cam Talbot has been steady, and the team has allowed about two fewer goals than expected. Zach Werenski and Damon Severson carry the blue line, 342 minutes together with a 20-11 goal edge. Up front, Knies and Kent Johnson have been good with Luca Del Bel Belluz between them (56% of the expected goals, 7-2 in goals) and merely even with Adam Fantilli.

The trouble is the hole. Even with the luck owed to them, our numbers put Columbus's playoff chances at 7%. What we'd watch: whether the shooting turns before the season gets away completely.
